title: AD Permission Gauntlet
description: GenericAll → ForceChangePassword → Password Safe → Targeted Kerberoast → DCSync. Pure BloodHound-driven chain.
introduction: Teaches AD permission abuse without exploits: GenericAll, ForceChangePassword, GenericWrite on SPN. BloodHound reveals the path; bloodyAD executes it. No RCE needed—just LDAP.
mental_model: AD objects have permissions. GenericAll = full control; ForceChangePassword = set password; GenericWrite on user = add SPN for Kerberoast. Chain permission → new cred → next permission.
key_principles: BloodHound/SharpHound map permission paths to DA
GenericAll or ForceChangePassword lets you set a known password
Password Safe = LDAP cred store; bloodyAD get object retrieves it
GenericWrite on user + add SPN = Targeted Kerberoast (no crack needed)
DCSync with DA hash dumps entire domain credential database

vulnerabilities.summary: SMB with domain creds for enumeration

services.name: LDAP
commands: bloodyAD -d domain.local -u olivia -p '<password>' --host 10.10.11.42 get object michael --attr msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity

vulnerabilities.summary: Targeted Kerberoast after GenericWrite on ethan SPN

credentials.source: GenericWrite on ethan → add SPN → Targeted Kerberoast

commands: bloodyAD -d domain.local -u olivia -p '<password>' --host 10.10.11.42 set password michael 'NewPassword123!' --new-password
bloodyAD -d domain.local -u emily -p '<password>' --host 10.10.11.42 add spn ethan 'ops/whatever'

attack_paths.name: AD Permission Chain (Primary)
attack_paths.description: olivia (given) → GenericAll michael → ForceChangePassword → michael → ForceChangePassword benjamin → benjamin → Password Safe → emily → GenericWrite ethan (SPN) → Targeted Kerberoast ethan → ethan is DA → DCSync
